string-array.name: changelog_items
string-array.item: An empty argument to a11y text is now a legal input meaning "clear this field" (no need to find and press that clear button, which often has no node name at all). Clearing goes through ACTION_SET_TEXT only: pasting an empty clipboard is a no-op on most hosts while performAction still reports true, which would turn into "the reply says ok but the field is still full"; when it cannot be cleared the answer is an honest set_text_rejected. The CLI test changed from the truthiness of a[1] to the argument count (truthiness judged a11y text with an empty argument as missing arguments and printed usage - which is exactly how clearing a field was locked out).

The bugreport dialog now discloses what goes into the archive: it includes the capability-call log (which capability was called when, and what came back), with notification bodies, SMS, clipboard and spoken text masked, while shell commands and accessibility actions are kept as they are. Until now "the report carries the capability-call log" was only written in the file header - that is for whoever reads the report, not for whoever presses send.

The bugreport now carries audit-log.txt: the capability-call audit (the same data as the on-device "privilege call log" - who called what, when, and what came back) goes into the archive. It exists because of the last accessibility report: "the service cannot find the string it just wrote with --target" and "--class says nothing matched while the node is right there in the tree" were one glance away with it (request params, status code, response body), and the report carried none of it, so that round was spent asking back and guessing. On privacy it collects only the field each endpoint declares as its masking policy (notification bodies, SMS, clipboard and TTS are masked; shell and accessibility are not, by design, because what the user reviews is where it tapped and what it typed); the unmasked copy of the same params (fullCommand) is not exported with the report. The current file keeps its last 500 entries and the rotated previous one its last 200 (the incident entries often live there), truncation is written into the file header, and it is redacted like every other collected item.

Two real-device bugs in accessibility addressing were fixed, plus one risk tier: (1) --target/--class used to search only the active window while writing goes through the input-focus window - on a real device those can differ (one run had input.window=29546 next to rootWindow=1), so the service could not find the text it had just written with --target. It now searches every readable window in a fixed order (active, input focus, screen-reader focus, then the rest, always skipping our own overlay window); not_found carries searchedWindows (which windows were actually read) and matches, and tree always carries windows[]; (2) a11y text gained --index N (same meaning as click), so "I want the second field" is finally expressible on a page with two inputs; (3) typing and system actions counted as the dangerous tier, which by design always asks - adding accessibility to "no more asking" therefore still prompted on every call, leaving that list useless for accessibility. The criterion goes back to the one the read/write tiering uses: they change screen state but none is unrecoverable (tap/click were already writes and can press any send/delete button), and the dangerous tier stays for uninstall, reboot and wiping data. Adding accessibility to the list now silences the whole family.

After a device report that no input field could be written to at all, four things were fixed along the verified conclusions: (1) the focus path now has three layers (system resolution by the input-focus window, then asking the tree we picked, then the first visible editable node in it) - AOSP voids the first query entirely when that window does not belong to the caller display type, which a window on the mirror virtual display hits, and the old code answered no_input_focus right there; (2) when SET_TEXT is refused it falls back to focus + clipboard + PASTE, and the reply says which path ran via by:set_text / by:paste (the clipboard is restored afterwards) - an accessibility service cannot reach the target app InputConnection, that API does not exist in AOSP; (3) the diagnostics stopped being lossy: input (FOCUS_INPUT) and a11y (FOCUS_ACCESSIBILITY, the screen-reader cursor) are reported separately with the id of the window that answered each, the tree reports rootWindow/rootChildren, and failures gained windowReadable plus per-window id/type/rootAvailable (which tells a missing root apart from an empty package name); (4) clicking a node that only reports a degenerate rectangle (zero width, or off screen) now answers invalid_bounds instead of silently tapping a line.

The plugin page gained Userscripts: import a .user.js (paste it, or pick a file) and it runs before the page own scripts, so it can change the UI of the web page this app shows - an extension point with no packaging and no release. The metadata block, @match / @include / @exclude and @run-at (document-start / -end / -idle) are read the Greasemonkey way, and GM_getValue / setValue / deleteValue, GM_addStyle, GM_log and GM_notification (which lands as a system toast) are available. Every script is injected as its own piece, so one broken script leaves the others alone, and a master switch plus a per-script switch take it all back at any time (the manager is native, so it still opens when a script blanks the WebView). This app own page only.

Better accessibility ergonomics: (1) typing into a field can now address it with just `--class` — an input inside a WebView usually has neither text nor a view id, so the class (e.g. EditText) is the only handle; (2) a locator that matches nothing is now `not_found`, separate from `no_input_focus` (both used to answer the latter, so "nothing matched" read like "no focus"); (3) the node tree gained `focused` (who holds keyboard focus), `input` (what focus resolves to) and `own` (the active window was our own overlay), and failures carry `window`/`windows[]` — one run on a device separates "the service sees the target app" from "it sees our own window"; (4) the web inputs of the app itself now carry a name (the placeholder the page already shows becomes an aria-label), so the agent can find them by name from the tree.

The "no more asking" list is now managed in one place: a new category at the bottom of Permissions lists every native capability by category (searchable by capability name, summary or category name), and switched on means it is no longer asked one by one. The switch used to sit on each capability card — which meant it was not a list at all: you could not see what you had exempted, and adding one meant finding its card first.

Fixed the accessibility screenshot (a11y screenshot): the service config was missing the canTakeScreenshot declaration. That one is a hard requirement and is read only when the system binds the service — without it the system throws a SecurityException on the server side and the user just sees a vague "capture failed". It is declared now, and the error codes the system returns are translated into actionable reasons (the 333ms minimum gap waits and retries once; a stale capability answers no_screenshot_capability, fixable by toggling the accessibility switch off and on).

New "Virtual screens" manager (Settings → Security → Permissions → Virtual screen → Manage virtual screens): it lists **every** virtual screen still alive in the server (id, size, dpi, whether a picture is being sent, which app is running on it), with per-screen preview and terminate, plus terminate-all. Changing the size made the agent create an extra screen and the old one never went away, with nowhere for the user to see it — this is that place. It does not start the server just to show the list.

The permission dialog gained a third answer: "Allow and stop asking". Strictness used to be **global**, so the only way to stop the virtual screen from prompting on every tap was dropping the whole device to normal/loose — which also frees up shell, SMS, notifications and everything else. This no-more-asking list works **per capability** and can be revoked any time from that capability\'s card in Settings → Security → Permissions; dangerous actions (uninstall, reboot, wiping data) ignore it and always ask. The virtual screen\'s risk is now graded per endpoint too (status and screenshot count as read-only, tap/swipe/key/launch as write), which is what makes "no dialog" actually reachable.

The permission settings are now a drill-down: the Security page keeps a single "Permissions" entry, and inside you pick a category (privileged channel, wireless ADB, native capabilities) or search a capability by name. Each capability\'s access level is picked from a sheet when you open its card, instead of a row of buttons.

New virtual screen: DSH can start an app on its own virtual display and operate it for you — screenshots, taps, swipes and key events — while your own screen stays where it is. Turn it on in Settings → Security → Permissions (Native capabilities → Screen and external UI → Virtual screen); it needs a privileged channel (root, Shizuku or wireless ADB).

New virtual screen preview (Settings → Security → Permissions → Screen and external UI → Virtual screen): watch the picture live and drive it by hand. Tap or swipe right on the video, use Back / Home / Recents, or type a package name to start it on that screen. It talks to the same service the agent uses, so it also tells you whether a problem sits on the picture side or the input side.

The agent now has a display tool with eight operations and matching dsh-native subcommands, documented in the host prompt. Viewing and acting are kept separate: with read-only access it can take screenshots but cannot touch anything.

Fixed a black-picture bug on the virtual screen: the codec setup was sent once, when the encoder started, so anything attaching later — which is how a preview always opens — received no SPS/PPS and stayed black, with no error reported anywhere. The frame stream is now self-contained.

Fixed dsh-native not being refreshed when the app is updated: with an existing container the old copy stayed in place, so subcommands the host prompt already advertised showed up to the agent as command not found.
Fixed changes under displayserver/ or tools/ not triggering a build, which let a server-side change land without ever being compiled.
The virtual screen is ported from Operit\'s shower subsystem (LGPL-3.0), itself derived from scrcpy (Apache-2.0); both credits are in the README and in the source.

Each privileged channel option now says exactly where it is stuck — not granted, not detected on this device, or never configured. Picking one that is not ready takes you straight to the step that fixes it (pair / request permission / verify / install the runtime) instead of just falling back with an unavailable notice. The Wireless ADB entry in Permissions also stays visible with its state, paired or not configured yet.

Native capabilities are regrouped into six categories: Interact with the device, Device and environment info, Personal content, Camera/mic and location, Screen and external UI, Privileges and system changes. The two screen-reading paths (accessibility and virtual screen) now have their own group instead of being buried in a ten-item list, and Install permission status moved out of Change system state into the read-only group it belongs to.

Fixed the virtual screen never starting in release builds: the server process did come up and its hand-over broadcast arrived on time, but the class it uses to hand over the binder had been renamed by release minification, so the app could not recognise it and then misreported the timeout as the server process not starting, pointing you at your device and elevation channel instead. That class name is now explicitly kept, and the failure message says plainly that it is a build configuration problem. BUG reports now also bundle the display server\'s own log, so this kind of problem no longer needs a round of questions.

Fixed a batch of container-side commands that could never work on a real device: `display status`, `display stop`, `a11y screenshot`, `device`, `clip get`, `tts voices`, `phone`, `sensors list`, `network`, `volume`, `settings` and `install` were missing the mandatory reason parameter, so every call came back `reason_required` and looked like an unimplemented feature. Usage is unchanged — you still pass `--reason` — they just actually get sent now.

The virtual screen no longer leaves one behind every time it is created: the same size and dpi now reuses the screen that already exists (each creation used to be a new one, reclaimed only on stop, so dumpsys accumulated a row of same-sized virtual screens). The preview page now attaches to the screen the agent is actually driving — it used to open its own, which left the user watching a blank screen while the agent tapped on a different one.
Settings → Permissions no longer opens with the search box already expanded and the keyboard covering the category list; tapping the magnifier starts a search.

New **virtual screen floating window**: while the agent drives a virtual screen, a collapsed handle appears at the screen edge showing the icon of the app it is driving — tap it to expand a live view. Before this, what it tapped and what the screen looked like was invisible unless you went and opened the preview page yourself. Once expanded it can be dragged and shown fullscreen, and tapping the picture reveals the controls (which hide themselves after 3 seconds). The form follows Operit: collapsed and out of the way by default, expands on tap, 300ms animations throughout. It needs the "display over other apps" permission (turn it on from Settings → Permissions → the virtual screen row; flipping the switch takes you to that system page). Without the permission the feature quietly does nothing and never affects the agent. Opening the full preview page makes it step aside, and it comes back when you close it.

Fixed **Enter only sending on phones, making multi-line messages impossible**: pressing Enter in the chat box sent the message immediately, and a newline required Shift+Enter — which a soft keyboard simply does not have, with no setting to change it (upstream registers Enter/Shift+Enter as read-only shortcuts). On touch screens Enter now inserts a newline and you send with the send button. Enter while your IME is composing, and Enter while the `/`, `@` or `+` menu is open, still behave as before (confirming a candidate / selecting an item). Turn it off in Settings → Features → WebUI compatibility; takes effect after a refresh.

Fixed a **floating window you could not get out of fullscreen**: the fullscreen state was missing the "tap the picture to show the controls" branch, so once you went fullscreen and the controls hid themselves, tapping did nothing — the whole screen stayed covered with no way to exit fullscreen or close it, and the only way out was restarting the app. Entering and leaving fullscreen now shows the controls immediately, and the controls stay the same three icons (collapse / fullscreen / close). Video rendering moved to TextureView so the window can finally have rounded corners (SurfaceView is composited as its own layer, so parent clipping has no effect and the corners stay square).

The floating window can now **operate the virtual display while in fullscreen**: taps and swipes are forwarded into that display (the coordinate mapping and the "is this a tap or a swipe" threshold are the same ones the preview page uses). In the small-window state it still only watches — there a tap brings up the controls. Because single-finger touches in fullscreen all go to the virtual display and the overlay never sees them, the fullscreen controls became a small **always-on** pill in the top-right (collapse / exit fullscreen / close) so there is always a way out.

The virtual-screen window no longer fails to appear: it used to be synced only at the **create-session** step, so when the agent kept working on an existing screen with an explicit `--display N`, the window never showed up. Any successful display command now brings it up. The handle is no longer invisible either — it fades in, lights up every time the agent uses the screen, and explains itself once the first time it appears. Its ✕ now **terminates that virtual screen** (it asks first, because the agent\'s next step will fail); the "just hide it" action moved to the collapse button on the controls. To go with that, omitting `--display` no longer falls back to the real screen: with no session you get an explicit `no_session`.

A way to judge "it feels laggy": while the window is expanded, one line under the controls shows the video link\'s numbers (queued/decoded fps, dropped frames, peak queue depth, average wait), and the same line is logged every 2 seconds.
